title: Snapdragon X Elite original-weight CPU SIMD: paired 80B MTP4 validation and timing
scope: One native Windows ARM64 laptop; candidate adds batched integer expert kernels, exact four-row DeltaNet FP16-state updates, and exact four-row FP16 routing. Every fresh and warm process sample is retained. No accelerator execution or reduced weight precision is used.
path_policy: Project-relative paths; user-profile absolute paths and OS process/thread identifiers removed. Measurement values, counters and hashes retained.

hardware.os_execution: Native Windows ARM64; WSL used for cross-building and host checks, not timed model inference

changes: ARM I8MM batched expert kernels retain original integer block arithmetic and scaling.
DeltaNet processes four independent rows with scalar-order FP32 reductions, separate multiply/add and final-only FP16 state rounding; persistent row-major state/replay layout unchanged.
Router processes four independent rows; a lossless FP16 interleave borrows unused space in resident F32 tensors without changing row-major GPU inputs or allocating additional router heap.

models.name: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
models.precision: Original Q4_K_M quantized weights; Janas planes preserve original quantized bits. HIGH quality, expert bits 6, head bits 0, no expert skipping.

jns_mtp_sidecar.note: Separate Q4_K MTP heads; official main GGUF omits them. Janas reports the distinct sidecar cache separately.

models.verification: Full SHA verified during original downloads; not rescanned here to avoid warming payload. Sizes and mtimes recorded.

controls.os_file_cache: uncontrolled across sequential processes; fresh does not mean cold SSD
controls.comparison_gate: all A/B output hash and count signatures agree per workload; strict logit/state quality gates coordinated separately

protocol.code_and_prose: ABBA; two fresh processes and five warm samples per binary/workload, split3+2 warm rounds across its processes.
protocol.long_prompt: AB; one fresh process and three warm samples per binary.
protocol.sample_scope: Each sample starts a new chat with no prompt KV reuse; only warm samples reuse the same process's private expert cache.
protocol.file_cache_scope: OS file cache uncontrolled across sequential processes. Fresh process does not mean cold SSD.
protocol.io_counter_scope: Expert byte counts are logical file reads, not measured physical SSD traffic or throughput.

counter_semantics.sample_scalar_expert_fields: expert_requests/hits/misses, demand/prefetch/warm/logical bytes and I/O/wait seconds are per-sample deltas summed over main plus distinct MTP cache; expert_counters_scope labels that combined storage scope.
counter_semantics.nested_expert_cache: Each sample retains counter_scope=sample_delta. Requests, hits, misses, logical bytes, prefetch counts and I/O/wait seconds are deltas; capacity_bytes and arena_bytes are end-of-sample gauges. Setup records retain their own cache_lifetime tag.
counter_semantics.accelerator_counters: Sample work/plan counters retain count_scope=sample_delta; setup counters retain model_lifetime. npu_weight_bytes is always a current_unique_resident gauge, rather than a sample delta.
counter_semantics.io_seconds: Sum of cache read wall times; overlapping I/O means this is not physical SSD service time or bandwidth.
counter_semantics.peak_rss: Process-lifetime high-water mark, not per-sample memory usage.

protocol.memory_scope: Peak RSS is process lifetime; expert-cache capacities separately report main and distinct MTP storage.
protocol.payload_verification: Full SHA verified during original downloads; not rescanned here to avoid warming payload. Sizes and mtimes recorded.

code.aggregation: ratio of medians over all retained warm samples for each binary; not paired per-round division

prose.aggregation: ratio of medians over all retained warm samples for each binary; not paired per-round division

long.aggregation: ratio of medians over all retained warm samples for each binary; not paired per-round division

telemetry.timestamp_scope: Written after the single read-only WMI query; not synchronized with an individual sample
telemetry.limits: One aggregate-frequency snapshot does not establish thermal throttling, a root cause of rate variation, or per-core clocks. Existing unrelated applications were left running. Benchmark builds and other model inference were idle.

measurement_observation.interpretation: Sustained trials exhibited variable absolute CPU performance. The single aggregate WMI snapshot was not synchronized to a sample and cannot establish thermal throttling, per-core clocks, or the cause of rate variation. This report compares only the contemporaneous A/B cases; historical throughput figures are not controls.

functional_and_numerical_validation.boundary: Exactness established for the listed fixtures and kernel tests; no pruning, new activation quantization or lower weight precision is enabled. No claim of exhaustive model-quality evaluation.

supplemental_microbenchmarks.scope: Preliminary isolated kernel checks performed under concurrent validation CPU load; these are not end-to-end model speedups and must not be multiplied into workload results.

experts.provenance: Two baseline and two candidate kernel samples per vector count under concurrent validation; not paired model results. Ratio is baseline median seconds divided by candidate median seconds.

limits: Single laptop, short fixed workloads and small sample counts; no confidence interval or universal speed claim.
Thermal/power state and OS file-cache effects can vary; alternating ABBA order reduces order bias but does not eliminate it.
Different process cache warmth changes fresh-process latency; compare the explicitly labeled warm medians separately.
No new GPU/NPU acceleration claim is made by this CPU-only experiment.
Kernel-only supplemental timings were collected under concurrent validation load and cannot predict end-to-end gains.

deployment_validation.scope: Focused local server functional and thread-placement validation after the CPU SIMD measurements. The original paired process cases, medians, ratios, binary identities and quality records are unchanged.

engine_source_identity_at_validation.note: Both raw and LF-normalized identities are recorded to distinguish line-ending changes; no circular future commit reference.

readiness.boundary: Direct local API and served page HTTP; no browser interaction, document retrieval or RAG validation.

code_api_request.timing_scope: Single functional HTTP request; not the paired benchmark or a controlled performance comparison.

active_thread_placement.scope: Read-only Toolhelp/GetThreadGroupAffinity and thread CPU-time snapshot; chronological indices are local ordering, not OS thread identifiers.
active_thread_placement.inference_caller_identification: The unique later-created thread with the opening thread mask and more than 0.2 CPU seconds, active alongside seven distinct other pinned compute workers; consistent with the engine affinity handoff.

observed_thread_placement.scope: Read-only Toolhelp/GetThreadGroupAffinity and thread CPU-time snapshot; chronological indices are local ordering, not OS thread identifiers.

result.timing_scope: Single functional HTTP request; not the paired benchmark or a controlled performance comparison.
Single functional HTTP request; not the paired benchmark or a controlled performance comparison.

before_handoff_diagnostic.bounded_finding: The observed pre-fix opening thread had mask 0x10 while a later active inference caller had mask 0xff; seven other workers were individually pinned. This was a caller-placement mismatch, not a collapse of the pool onto one CPU.
before_handoff_diagnostic.timing_limit: The two pre-fix functional requests had widely different output times of 51.9177134s and 9.5307952s. Their differences, and the final 6.8573835s request, do not establish a causal speedup from the affinity fix; cache warmth, order and runtime conditions were uncontrolled.

focused_affinity_regression.scope: No-model engine affinity regression, separate from the earlier 51 native programs and 52 sanitizer-suite programs.
focused_affinity_regression.negative_control_change: Temporary source outside the repository removed only engine-entry affinity restoration. Both platforms detected the missing model-opening mask handoff and exited 1 as expected. Existing production binaries and source were preserved.

limits: A single functional API request is not a throughput benchmark and does not replace the retained paired results.
The query-only five-second sample establishes the recorded active masks and CPU-time bound, not scheduling placement for every future request or context.
The opening thread mask was transferred as captured; CPU 0 was not hardcoded.
No causal performance ratio is inferred from before/after API timings.
